audit.title: Chainlink Data Streams

dimensions.name: Answer-first extractability
dimensions.analysis: Strong. Opens with a crisp canonical claim: "Chainlink Data Streams delivers low-latency market data offchain, which you can verify onchain." Most sections lead with a standalone statement. No action needed beyond the specifics injection below.

dimensions.name: Structural scannability & chunkability
dimensions.analysis: Strong. 10 headings, clean H1→H3, 0 level skips, sections median 69 words (max 126) — ideal RAG chunk sizes. Weak spot: the "Comparison to push-based oracles" section is prose where a table would extract better (0 tables on page).

dimensions.name: Concrete statistics & specifics
dimensions.analysis: Weak. Only "sub-second" and "99.9%+ uptime" quantify anything; latency, frequency, report-format count, and connection counts are all qualitative. "several report formats," "robust fault tolerance" beg for numbers.

dimensions.name: Citations & authoritative references
dimensions.analysis: Developing. 18 internal links are good for hub navigation, but 0 external/primary sources — no link to a whitepaper, spec, or canonical definition to anchor credibility.

dimensions.name: Quotable canonical definitions
dimensions.analysis: Good. Pull-vs-push and commit-and-reveal are both cleanly defined verbatim ("A 'commit-and-reveal' approach mitigates frontrunning by making trade data and stream data visible atomically onchain").

dimensions.name: Machine-readability & metadata
dimensions.analysis: Weak. Measured: 0 JSON-LD blocks, canonical MISSING, no datePublished/dateModified, 0 og/twitter tags. No `TechArticle` schema or visible freshness signal. (Head was not captured — CLI should pass raw `<head>` to confirm.)

dimensions.name: Code completeness & agent-runnability
dimensions.analysis: Weak for an integration-adjacent page. 0 code fences. Acceptable for a pure overview, but a single "fetch and verify a report" snippet would let agents act without a second hop.

dimensions.name: Query/intent coverage
dimensions.analysis: Developing. Covers "what is," "how to use," and use cases, and has a numbered getting-started path. No troubleshooting/FAQ and no symptom-phrased headings.

dimensions.name: Clarity, fluency & terminology consistency
dimensions.analysis: Strong. Consistent naming (Data Streams, DON, pull-based), unambiguous prose. No action needed.

audit.summary: This is a well-written top-of-funnel overview page for Chainlink Data Streams: clean prose, a strong liftable opening definition, and a logical section hierarchy with 18 internal links routing to SDKs and reference docs. Its biggest GEO strength is answer-first extractability — nearly every section leads with a self-contained claim. Its biggest opportunities are concrete specifics (only 5 numerals, none with units, plus vague quantifiers "several/some/robust") and machine-readable metadata (no JSON-LD, missing canonical, no dates). The honest verdict: a solid navigational hub that under-delivers on the quantitative detail and structured metadata that generative engines reward most.

recommendations.title: Inject concrete numbers into capability claims
recommendations.change: State exact figures: median/target latency in ms, report update frequency, the actual number of report formats/asset classes, and supported networks. Replace "several report formats" with e.g. "N report schemas (v3 crypto, v4 RWA, …)".
recommendations.why: Quantitative claims are the highest-lift retrievable content; engines preferentially cite pages with specific numbers over qualitative prose.

recommendations.title: Add `TechArticle` JSON-LD, canonical URL, and last-updated date
recommendations.issue: Measured: 0 JSON-LD, canonical MISSING, no dateModified.
recommendations.change: Emit a `TechArticle` block with `headline`, `dateModified`, `about: "Chainlink Data Streams"`, and a self-referential canonical link.
recommendations.why: Structured metadata and visible freshness raise agent trust and E-E-A-T parseability; canonical prevents .md/.html duplication ambiguity.

recommendations.title: Convert push-vs-pull comparison into a table
recommendations.issue: Reasons are buried in prose ("Some applications only need onchain data at fixed intervals…").
recommendations.change: Add a 2-column table (Push-based | Data Streams / pull-based) with rows for update trigger, latency, cost model, verification, best-fit use case.
recommendations.why: Tables let engines extract *reasons* and build justified comparative answers ("which oracle for perps?").

recommendations.title: Add symptom/question-phrased headings and a short FAQ
recommendations.issue: No content phrased as the questions devs ask.
recommendations.change: Add H3s like "What's the difference between Data Feeds and Data Streams?", "How do I verify a report onchain?", "Which SDK should I use?" with 1–2 sentence liftable answers linking to the deep pages.
recommendations.why: Question-phrased headings win retrieval that concept-titled prose loses, even when the body already contains the answer.

recommendations.title: Add one minimal end-to-end code example
recommendations.where: "How to use Data Streams" → Integration options
recommendations.issue: 0 code blocks; agents must navigate away to act.
recommendations.change: Add a short, language-tagged snippet (e.g. Go SDK) showing fetch → decode → onchain-verify, with imports, that links to the full tutorial.
recommendations.why: Copy-pasteable, labeled snippets are directly liftable by coding agents completing tasks.

recommendations.title: Add external/primary references
recommendations.issue: 0 external links; claims like "active-active multi-site deployment" are self-referential only.
recommendations.change: Link the first mention of DON to its canonical concept/whitepaper, and any latency/uptime SLA claim to a spec or status page.
recommendations.why: Inline authoritative references raise citation rate and make quantitative claims attributable.

recommendations.title: Replace vague quantifiers
recommendations.issue: vague quantifiers flagged: several, some, robust.
recommendations.change: Swap for specifics (e.g. "fault tolerance across N isolated origins").
recommendations.why: Qualitative hedges underperform; specificity is independently rewarded.

antiPatterns: Vague quantifiers: "several report formats," "some applications," "robust fault tolerance."
Two `(Image: Image)` placeholders with no alt text — no textual value for engines; add descriptive captions.
No dated/freshness signal (dateModified absent) — undated content is a mild trust penalty.
No keyword stuffing, no marketing fluff of note, no broken cross-references. Prose is clean.
offPageNotes: `llms.txt` is already referenced at the top — good site-level signal; ensure it lists this page as the Data Streams canonical hub.
Head metadata could not be verified from the supplied content; the CLI should pass raw `<head>` so JSON-LD/canonical/OG presence can be confirmed rather than inferred.
Site-level: ensure sitemap and internal links from sibling reference pages point back to this overview to reinforce it as the canonical entry point (canonical-hub pattern).
